title: Set 109

sentences.ko: 애가 잠들 때까지 침대 옆에 누워 있으라고 해서 누워 있었는데, 내가 먼저 잠든 게 거의 확실해. 정신 차려 보니 아홉 시 반이고 폰은 바닥에 떨어져 있더라고. 믿고 있던 저녁 시간이 통째로 날아간 거지. 그런데 내일 애 도시락도 아직 싸야 해.
sentences.text: She made me lie down next to her bed until she fell asleep, and I'm pretty sure I went out before she did, because the next thing I knew it was nine thirty and my phone was on the floor. So the whole evening I was counting on is just gone. And I still have to pack her lunch for tomorrow.

alts.text: I had to lie down next to her bed till she konked out, and I'm pretty sure I went out first, because next thing I know it's nine thirty and my phone's on the floor. So there goes the whole evening I was counting on. And I still gotta pack her lunch for tomorrow.

She insisted that I lie down beside her bed until she fell asleep, and I am fairly certain I fell asleep before she did, because the next thing I knew it was nine thirty and my phone was on the floor. So the entire evening I had been counting on is simply gone. And I still need to pack her lunch for tomorrow.

sentences.note: **went out** 은 밖에 나갔다는 뜻이 아니라 곯아떨어졌다는 말입니다. **the next thing I knew** 는 정신을 차려 보니라는 뜻이고, **counting on** 은 그것만 믿고 기대하고 있었다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 여보세요, 뒤쪽 집에 사는 댄인데요. 안방에 난방이 안 들어와요. 주말부터 계속 그래서 거기에 전기 난로를 켜 놓고 있는데, 그거 싫어하시는 거 저도 알아요. 다른 데는 다 멀쩡한 걸 보면 전체가 고장 난 것 같지는 않고요. 진짜 추워지기 전에 이번 주에 누가 한번 와서 봐 주실 수 있을까요?
sentences.text: Hey, it's Dan in the back unit. The heat's not kicking on in the bedroom, and it's been like that since the weekend, so we've had a space heater going in there, which I know you don't love. Everywhere else in the place is fine, so I don't think it's the whole system. Is there any chance somebody could come look at it this week, before it really gets cold?

alts.text: Hey, Dan in the back unit. Bedroom heat's not coming on, and it's been like that since the weekend, so we've had a space heater running in there, which I know you're not a fan of. Rest of the place is fine, so I don't think it's the whole system. Any chance someone could take a look this week, before it really gets cold?

Hello, this is Dan in the back unit. The heat is not turning on in the bedroom, and it has been that way since the weekend, so we have been running a space heater in there, which I know you would rather we not do. Everywhere else in the unit is fine, so I do not believe it is the entire system. Would it be possible for someone to come look at it this week, before it truly gets cold?

sentences.note: **kicking on** 은 난방이나 기계가 켜져서 돌아가기 시작한다는 뜻입니다. **you don't love** 는 싫어한다는 말을 부드럽게 돌려 말한 것이고, **Is there any chance** 는 조심스럽게 부탁할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 토요일에 봄 이후로 처음으로 친구들이랑 농구를 했는데, 하는 내내 몸이 아주 좋았거든. 그게 핵심이야. 문제는 오늘이지. 오늘 아침에 계단 오를 엄두가 안 나서 한 층 가는데 엘리베이터를 탔는데, 누가 같이 타는 바람에 서서 왜 탔는지 해명을 해야 했어.
sentences.text: I played basketball with the guys on Saturday for the first time since the spring, and I felt great the whole time, that's the thing. It's today that's the problem. I took the elevator up one floor this morning because I couldn't face the stairs, and somebody got in with me, so I had to stand there and explain myself.

alts.text: So I got out and played basketball with the guys Saturday, first time since spring, and I felt great the whole time, that's the thing. It's today that's the problem. Took the elevator up one floor this morning because I couldn't deal with the stairs, and somebody got in with me, so I'm standing there explaining myself.

I played basketball with some friends on Saturday for the first time since the spring, and I felt wonderful throughout, which is the strange part. It is today that is the problem. I took the elevator up a single floor this morning because I could not bring myself to take the stairs, and someone stepped in with me, so I had to stand there and explain myself.

sentences.note: **that's the thing** 은 바로 그 점이 핵심이라고 짚을 때 씁니다. **couldn't face the stairs** 는 계단을 오를 엄두가 안 났다는 뜻이고, **explain myself** 는 내가 왜 그랬는지 해명한다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 여동생이 다음에 뭘 할지 정할 때까지 몇 달만 나랑 같이 지내면 안 되냐고 물어봤어. 생각해 보겠다고 했는데, 그게 결국 그러자는 뜻인 건 둘 다 알지. 근데 우리 집은 좁고, 같이 살아 본 게 내가 열아홉 살 때가 마지막이야. 안 된다고 해도 걔는 아무렇지 않을 거야. 걸리는 건 그게 아니야. 나 때문에 걔가 부모님한테 가서 부탁하게 되는 게 싫은 거지.
sentences.text: My sister asked if she could stay with me for a few months while she figures out her next thing, and I told her I'd think about it, which we both know means I'm going to say yes. But my place is small, and the last time we lived together I was nineteen. If I said no she'd be fine about it, that's not even what I'm stuck on. I just don't want to be the reason she has to go ask my parents instead.

alts.text: So my sister wants to crash with me for a few months while she figures out her next thing, and I said I'd think about it, which we both know means yes. But my place is tiny, and last time we lived together I was nineteen. If I said no she'd be fine, that's not even what I'm stuck on. I just don't wanna be the reason she has to go ask my parents instead.

My sister asked whether she might stay with me for a few months while she determines her next step, and I told her I would think about it, which we both know means I am going to say yes. But my apartment is small, and the last time we lived together I was nineteen. If I declined she would be perfectly fine about it, and that is not even what I am stuck on. I simply do not want to be the reason she has to go ask my parents instead.

sentences.note: **figures out her next thing** 은 다음에 뭘 할지 정한다는 뜻입니다. **I'd think about it** 은 생각해 보겠다면서 답을 미루는 말이고, **what I'm stuck on** 은 마음에 걸려서 결정을 못 하는 지점을 가리킵니다.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 아니야, 우리 여기 잘 지내. 진짜로. 일은 바쁜데 하루가 빨리 가는 쪽으로 바빠서 오히려 괜찮아. 응, 저번에 전화했을 때 목소리가 피곤하게 들린 거 알아. 그냥 한 주가 길어서 그랬어. 아빠한테 일요일에 전화드린다고 전해 줘. 그리고 내가 가서 잡아 드릴 때까지 또 그 사다리에 올라가시게 두지 마.
sentences.text: No, we're good here, really. Work's busy, but it's the kind of busy where the day goes fast, so I'll take it. Yeah, I know I sounded tired when you called the other day, that was just the end of a long week. Tell Dad I'll call him Sunday, and don't let him get up on that ladder again before I'm there to hold it.

alts.text: Nah, we're good here, honestly. Work's busy, but it's the good kind where the day flies by, so I'll take it. Yeah, I know I sounded beat when you called the other day, that was just the end of a long week. Tell Dad I'll call him Sunday, and don't let him get back up on that ladder before I'm there to hold it.

No, we are doing well here, truly. Work is busy, but it is the sort of busy that makes the day pass quickly, so I will take it. Yes, I know I sounded tired when you called the other day; that was simply the end of a long week. Please tell Dad I will call him on Sunday, and do not let him get up on that ladder again before I am there to hold it.

sentences.note: **I'll take it** 은 완벽하진 않아도 그 정도면 받아들이겠다는 뜻입니다. **sounded tired** 는 목소리가 지쳐 들렸다는 말이고, 캐주얼의 **beat** 도 몹시 지쳤다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

reviewed: 1번 캐주얼의 "I went first" 가 무엇을 먼저 했다는 건지 두 가지로 읽혀서 "I went out first" 로 고쳤습니다 (본문의 went out 과도 맞습니다).
2번 캐주얼 첫머리 "Hi, this is Dan" 이 본문의 "Hey, it's Dan" 보다 오히려 격식 있어서 "Hey, Dan in the back unit" 으로 바꿨습니다.
2번 격식체의 "you would prefer we did not" 가 말끝이 잘린 듯 어색해서 "you would rather we not do" 로 고쳤습니다.
3번 격식체의 "the fellows" 는 요즘 원어민이 친구를 가리킬 때 쓰지 않는 낡은 말이라 "some friends" 로 바꿨습니다.
3번 격식체의 "which is the remarkable part" 는 본문 "that's the thing" 의 뜻(바로 그 점이 핵심)과 달라서 "which is the strange part" 로 고쳤습니다.
